core.title: Give each implemented user/system flow its own user/system flow URN line on the theme orchestrator
core.given: A theme orchestrator file for a theme exists or is planned, and it implements one or more user/system flows.
core.when: Any planning artifact or doc you author creates, changes (including internal-logic edits) or describes that orchestrator, or you find it missing URN lines.
core.then: Ensure the theme orchestrator file carries one user/system flow URN binding line per implemented user/system flow, with the URN's theme segment matching the orchestrator's theme.
prefer: When one orchestrator implements several user/system flows, plan multiple URN binding lines, one for each user/system flow.
When an existing orchestrator lacks a URN line for a user/system flow it implements, plan the missing line as part of the work.
avoid: A single combined line, or one that is not a well-formed user/system flow URN, standing in for several user/system flows.
User/system flow URNs whose theme segment differs from the orchestrator's theme.
URN lines for user/system flows the orchestrator does not actually implement, added only to satisfy a check.
core.why: The user/system flow URN's theme segment is what ties each implemented user/system flow to its theme orchestrator file, so every implemented user/system flow must be traceable by its own URN line.
evidence: For each theme orchestrator file, every implemented user/system flow has exactly one user/system flow URN binding line.
The theme segment of each URN equals the theme the orchestrator file is responsible for.
verification: The check pairs each theme orchestrator file with the user/system flows it implements and requires exactly one matching user/system flow URN binding line per implemented user/system flow; a missing line and a theme-segment mismatch are both findings.

The check is unconditional on file contents: it examines all theme orchestrator files, existing and new, regardless of the kind of change that touched them (internal-logic edits and repairs included).
Not covered: user/system flows that are registered but implemented by no orchestrator file (no orchestrator URN line is due for them), and files outside the theme orchestrator location.

values: orchestrator file missing a user/system flow URN line for an implemented user/system flow
URN theme segment differs from the orchestrator's theme

fires: A plan or product capability assigns a new user/system flow to a theme, so that theme's orchestrator file will implement it.
A planned orchestrator file implements several user/system flows of the same theme.
A plan creates a new theme orchestrator file.
A plan edits an existing orchestrator's internal logic: the file must still carry one URN line per implemented user/system flow.
An existing orchestrator file implements a user/system flow but lacks its user/system flow URN line (repair is required).
doesNotFire: Planning work touches only files outside the theme orchestrator location (e.g. product capability or user/system flow spec files themselves).
User/system flows that are registered but not implemented by any orchestrator file (no orchestrator URN line is due for them).

profileRequirements.meaning: The URN shape of a user/system flow; its theme segment identifies the theme an orchestrator URN line belongs to.
The syntax by which a theme orchestrator file carries a user/system flow URN line; this is the binding line the rule counts, one per implemented user/system flow.
Where theme orchestrator files live, one orchestrator per theme, with the theme identified by a {theme} placeholder in the path so the URN's theme segment can be matched to the file.
The suffix that identifies the theme orchestrator's file kind as production source, instantiating the core's file_kind activation fact; the Bun suffix list contains only this entry.

The language the theme orchestrator files are written in; the Bun fact's literal 'python' file-kind designation (note: 'Orchestrators are Python modules') names this language, which is separate from source-file identification by suffix.

bunOnly.text: Term orchestrator_urn: the theme-prefixed user/system flow URN on an orchestrator file; pattern user-system-flow:{theme}:{user_system_flow_id}.
bunOnly.reason: The term id of this one rule is a realization detail (core verification names the check generically); the concrete pattern is profile data (urn.user-system-flow).
Rule-specific example naming concrete URN and path values; bun.json itself is delivered as the worked reference example.
A literal binding-marker search term tied to the stack's line syntax; the marker syntax is profile data (urn.binding.user-system-flow), so the neutral core keeps only the conceptual task terms.

Finding values neutralized (pattern and filename replaced by user/system flow URN line and theme); the observer that pairs orchestrators with implemented user/system flows is described generically in verification.

neutralityNotes: 'user/system flow', 'theme', 'theme orchestrator' and 'product capability' are product concepts of the ATDD plan system, not stack concepts, so they stay in the core (the vocabulary already embraces them via urn.user-system-flow and layout.capability_dir). Everything stack-specific is data: the user/system flow URN shape (urn.user-system-flow), the binding-line syntax (urn.binding.user-system-flow), the orchestrator location and its {theme} name convention (roles.runtime_components#orchestrator_dir, proposed), the source-file suffix (suffix.source, suffix alone) and the orchestrator language (tooling.languages). How a file's theme is read off (filename stem) is Bun-specific and carried only by the layout pattern's placeholder; the term id orchestrator_urn, the example mapping and the literal 'urn:' search term remain realization details (bunOnly).
